eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Ten
subtitle: Lesson 94 · Performance Tuning · Chapter Finale

code:
-- Pulls every column, defeats a covering index
SELECT * FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail
WHERE SalesOrderID = 43659;

-- Name only what you need
SELECT SalesOrderID, ProductID, OrderQty, UnitPrice
FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail
WHERE SalesOrderID = 43659;
caption: A narrow covering index (Lesson 89) only helps if the query asks for exactly what it contains.

code:
-- Function wraps the column: no index can help
WHERE UPPER(LastName) = 'SMITH'

-- Type mismatch forces a conversion on every row
WHERE ProductID = '712'   -- ProductID is INT
caption: The #1 reason a "should be fast" query scans instead of seeks. Revisit Lesson 87.

eyebrow: Anti-pattern 3 — cursors instead of set-based logic
code:
-- Slow: one row at a time
DECLARE cur CURSOR FOR SELECT ProductID FROM Production.Product ...

-- Fast: the whole set, one operation
UPDATE Production.Product
SET ListPrice = ListPrice * 1.1
WHERE Color = 'Red';
caption: SQL Server is built to process sets, not loops. A cursor gives up that strength.

code:
-- Invoked once per row: a hidden cursor, and non-SARGable
WHERE dbo.udf_FiscalYear(OrderDate) = 2013

-- Rewritten as a plain, SARGable range
WHERE OrderDate >= '2012-07-01' AND OrderDate < '2013-07-01';
caption: Combines the worst of anti-patterns 2 and 3 — per-row overhead, and no index can help.
